says: Law 5's writer copies a real local home whole into fixtures/next/port-home, and a real home holds absolute machine paths: a failed span's stack text in brain.records.sqlite (table unsent, column content) and the built file's temp path in .alchemy/state/fabrika/local/Brain.json, so its output cannot be committed to this public repo as it is written.
proof: The one writer run allowed for S1 wrote a home whose brain.records.sqlite holds the brain.flush ControlError stack with the full path of the worktree under the account's home folder, and whose Brain.json props.main is a path under the system temp folder; leakgrep.sh --text on Brain.json exits 1 with machine_path at line 9. A git diff shows a .sqlite file only as binary, so the commit leak check would not see the first one.
cost: Law 5 stays red in CI until a home with no machine path is committed, and each later slice (S2, S3, S5, S8) that writes a new home meets the same leak, one the leak check cannot see inside SQLite.
